title: Runtime settings (P7)
note: Every timing and budget the specifications leave open, pinned in one place with a reason. Code carries no defaults for these (packages/engine/src/settings.ts refuses to start without them): a value that can silently fall back to something is a value nobody has decided. The `rationale` object mirrors the shape above it, one line per setting — a number without a reason is a number the next person will change by accident.

rationale.startupDeadlineSeconds: A Pod that has not reached Running in two minutes is not slow, it is stuck: image pull plus adapter start was measured well inside it.
rationale.terminationGraceSeconds: Enough for the adapter to flush its transcript after SIGTERM; the shutdown budget below is what actually bounds preservation.
rationale.inventoryFreshnessMs: How stale an owner inventory may be before a read is retaken. Shorter than one tick, so a tick never acts on evidence older than itself.
rationale.engine.claimLeaseMs: One claim covers a whole verb execution including an owner round trip. Long enough that a healthy worker never loses its own row mid-action, short enough that a dead worker's row is retried within a tick or two.
rationale.engine.claimLimit: Rows per scan. Bounded work per pass is what keeps one busy Workstream from starving the rest (ENGINE-016).
rationale.engine.tickPollIntervalMs: The floor on how often due work is noticed when no NOTIFY arrives. NOTIFY is the fast path; this is the one that survives a lost notification.
rationale.engine.sweepIntervalMs: Recovery sweeps re-enqueue Workstreams no wake reached. Rare by design: a sweep that runs often is hiding a missing wake hook.
rationale.engine.publicationBatchSize: Workstreams per enumeration and re-enqueue pass. One page must fit comfortably inside one transaction and one claim lease.
rationale.engine.publicationSweepIntervalMs: How often an interrupted publication is picked back up. It owes wakes, not urgency.
rationale.engine.backoff.baseDelayMs: First retry delay. Short enough that a transient owner error costs one second, not one tick.
rationale.engine.backoff.maxDelayMs: The cap. A minute is long enough to stop hammering a broken owner, short enough that recovery is not perceived as a hang.
rationale.engine.backoff.jitterRatio: Spreads retries so many Workstreams failing on the same owner do not resynchronize into a thundering herd.
rationale.engine.backoff.maxAttempts: After five failures the cause is not transient. The row stops retrying and says so, rather than spinning invisibly.
rationale.engine.backoff.recheckDelayMs: How often an exhausted row is looked at again — slow, but never never: the cause may have been fixed by someone else.
rationale.custody.preservationBudgetMs: The whole shutdown preservation window (OFF-001). Termination happens at the deadline whether or not a Save was captured; a larger value buys transcripts at the cost of leaving Pods alive longer.
rationale.custody.captureTimeoutMs: How long one driver capture may take inside that budget, leaving room for the Save commit and Anchor publication that follow.
rationale.custody.restoreTimeoutMs: A restore places one file; thirty seconds covers a slow store read, not a hung one.
rationale.custody.maxPayloadBytes: 32 MiB. A conversation transcript larger than this is a different problem than custody; the limit refuses the capture rather than growing the budget.
rationale.custody.captureStabilityWindowMs: Two reads this far apart must agree before a cut is called quiescent. Measured: a transcript keeps changing for ~100-200 ms after the process is killed.
rationale.custody.placementTimeoutMs: How long RESTORE waits for the Pod to place and verify the bytes before giving up for this tick. Not a failure — the next tick asks again.
rationale.custody.syncProofMaxAgeMs: How recent a driver verdict must be to count as current evidence. continuity.md asks for bounded current proof; this is the bound.
rationale.harness.seamPollIntervalMs: How often a Pod asks whether its gate opened. One second is imperceptible at launch and negligible in load.
rationale.harness.custodyPollIntervalMs: How often a Pod asks whether a capture, placement or proof is wanted. Also the floor on how fast a shutdown can get its answer.
rationale.harness.adapterHandshakeTimeoutMs: How long the bridge waits for the adapter's own initialize before declaring the process unusable.
rationale.engine.ownerRequestTimeoutMs: How long ONE owner call may take before the caller gives up and reports the field unavailable. It must stay under claimLeaseMs: an owner that never answers used to hang a tick for ever with the work row still claimed, which stops that Workstream reconciling at all — found live when a NetworkPolicy dropped (rather than refused) the Broker's packets.
rationale.harness.adapterRequestTimeoutMs: How long one ACP request to a harness adapter may take. An adapter that accepts a connection and never answers is indistinguishable from a slow one until this expires; without it a single unresponsive Pod froze the tick that probed it.
